top_issues.issue: Fissures and ore glow do not light the surrounding stone
top_issues.why: The brief's 04 reference is about fissures washing their stone; here each glow stays inside its own tile like a decal

top_issues.issue: Horizontal smear/streak texture on the rock faces
top_issues.why: It reads as a stretched noise texture rather than faceted low-poly stone and clashes with the chunky style
top_issues.suggested_direction: Replace it with per-face flat value variation or subtle facet normals; no stretched noise

top_issues.issue: Uniform block value, so the rock mass reads as a flat tiled sheet
top_issues.why: Reference 03 has strong per-cube value variation and lit vs shadowed faces that make the rock feel cubic
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add per-block value and hue jitter of roughly ±10–15%, plus a stronger top/side face contrast

top_issues.issue: Pocket backdrops are pure black and carry no haze
top_issues.why: The depth rule asks for a cooler, hazier background wall and black reserved for true void; the back wall barely separates from the void
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the back wall a faint world-tinted haze value just above black, still well under the lit foreground

protect: Strong one-hue-per-world rock palettes (amber, ice-blue, sea-green)

top_issues.issue: Ambient lift flattens the dark in the dense rock fields

top_issues.issue: Fissures still do not wash the neighbouring stone

top_issues.issue: No material distinction per world beyond hue

top_issues.issue: Fine grid/grain texture on the blocks is faint and slightly noisy

top_issues.suggested_direction: Either commit to visible facet breakup or drop it in favour of a flat per-face value

top_issues.issue: Fissures and ore glow without lighting the stone around them.

top_issues.issue: Wispy smoke streaks on the rock read as noise.

top_issues.issue: Depth bands within a world differ mainly in ore and fissure dressing; the palette and value shift between shallow and mid is minimal.
top_issues.why: The brief wants every depth to say which world it is. It does, but shallow and mid within one world are near-identical, so depth carries little identity of its own.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Shift each world's hue along depth: VEIL dusty rust to amber to ember-red, CRYOS pale ice to deep blue to cyan, MAELIS pale jade to deep green to nacre. Vary backdrop haze density per band.

top_issues.issue: The MAELIS core chamber drifts to lavender/grey.
top_issues.why: The one-hue-per-world rule breaks at the climax. The pearl's violet wash overrides sea-green, so the chamber does not read as MAELIS.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the pearl nacre-white with violet glints, but tint chamber haze, pillars and floor light toward sea-green. Add iridescent green/pink sheen rather than flat lilac.

top_issues.issue: Gold ore is the same in every world.
top_issues.why: A warm gold emissive sits in cold worlds and competes with the world hue at mid depth.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the ore's gameplay colour, but grade its halo toward the world hue, or swap in world-flavoured variants such as frost-gold or pearl-gold.

top_issues.issue: VEIL shallow and mid rock reads maroon/brown rather than amber.
top_issues.why: The target hue is amber/orange. Dull maroon makes the upper VEIL feel generic and drab next to 03-veil-mid's warm glints.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lift the lit-face hue toward amber and keep the dark faces deep. Let ore glints carry orange.

top_issues.issue: No nacre iridescence or hanging growth in MAELIS.
top_issues.why: 06-maelis is defined by nacre sheen and hanging strands. Without them MAELIS is just 'green CRYOS'.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a subtle view-angle hue shift on MAELIS lit faces and low-poly hanging strands from ceilings.

top_issues.issue: The backdrop world tint is largely removed. Backdrops are near-black, and the world hue sits only on the rock and pools.
top_issues.why: The tinted haze was the main carrier of 'which world am I in' at mid depth. Black backdrops make CRYOS and MAELIS mid frames read more alike.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the darker values, but put the world hue back into the dark: deep navy for CRYOS, deep bottle-green for MAELIS, deep rust for VEIL, instead of neutral black.

top_issues.issue: A warm/neutral beam desaturates the world hue on the surfaces it hits.
top_issues.why: The brightest area of the frame reads beige or khaki in the cold worlds, which contradicts the world palette right where the eye goes.

top_issues.issue: The MAELIS core chamber reads charcoal/violet.

top_issues.issue: Core chambers are less flooded with their hue.

top_issues.issue: Within-world depth bands are still near-identical apart from ore and fissure dressing.

top_issues.issue: Fissures don't light their stone

top_issues.issue: Lifted ambient backdrop flattens the dark around pools

top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop the cavity backdrop ambient toward near-black and let pool light, not ambient, reveal the back wall in a falloff gradient.

top_issues.issue: Core is a flat 2D disc

top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the core faceted geometry with internal shading under the bloom, and add a hotter floor pool directly beneath it.

top_issues.issue: Maelis core chamber loses world hue

top_issues.suggested_direction: Tint chamber haze sea-green, and keep the pearl's iridescence as a subtle rim shift rather than a lavender wash.

top_issues.issue: Fissures still don't light their stone

top_issues.issue: Backdrop goes neutral grey and loses world hue

top_issues.issue: Backdrop wall is evenly lit and as bright as or brighter than the footing
top_issues.why: The references keep the background cooler, hazier and darker so warm-lit platforms pop. Here dark-brown platforms sit on a lighter flat blue brick wall, which reverses that value order and flattens the depth.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Push the backdrop darker and hazier toward the edges, and let it brighten only inside sconce pools, so the foreground stone sits clearly in front.

top_issues.issue: Platform top faces aren't lit, so footing reads only by thin trim lines
top_issues.why: Readability of play is the top priority. Players should see walkable tops as the brightest edge of each slab, as in 08-vault-b.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give walkable top faces a consistent warm rim or lighter value, independent of nearby lights.

top_issues.issue: Light pools are sparse or missing in some rooms
top_issues.why: The brief asks for bronze sconces casting warm pools on masonry. The Return has almost no warm light, so it reads as a cold grey test room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add at least one or two sconces per screen in the sparse rooms, with a warm falloff on the surrounding stone.

top_issues.issue: The black spawn-gate box reads as a hole in the render
top_issues.why: A pure-black rectangle behind the player is used for something other than true void, and it competes with the figure.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the gate interior a dim tinted glow or a masonry frame so it reads as a doorway, not a cutout.

top_issues.issue: Floor hazards in the dark rooms are faint
top_issues.why: The fang strip along the bottom is dim against the near-black floor, so the hazard is less instantly legible than in the Ember rooms.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give fang tips a small emissive glow so they hold up in unlit rooms.

top_issues.suggested_direction: Darken and haze the backdrop away from light sources, and let only the sconce pools brighten it.

top_issues.issue: Sconce light reads as circular halos rather than light landing on masonry
top_issues.why: The brief asks for warm pools on stone. Whiter, rounder discs look like bloom sprites, not light falling on the wall.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep A's warmer, broader, directional falloff onto the masonry.

top_issues.issue: Platform top faces aren't lit, so footing reads only by thin trim
top_issues.why: Footing legibility is non-negotiable.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give walkable tops a consistent light rim or value lift.

top_issues.issue: Rooms are sparse or unlit
top_issues.why: With no warm sources, the room loses the vault mood entirely.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add sconces with warm pools to the Return rooms.

top_issues.issue: Floor fangs are faint in the dark rooms
top_issues.why: In unlit rooms the fangs are harder to spot than in the Ember rooms.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add an emissive glow to the fang tips.

per_shot.note: Strong wide-tracked wordmark with soft glow and restrained amber CTA, but it sits over a flat brown block wall with the surface base on top; nothing reads as a dark shaft with warm light rising from below, as in 01-title.
Minimal corner HUD (thin teal/red bars, centred depth, amber lumens) stays out of the dusk scene and the signage is legible; the bars are generic and the top-left labels are small.
HUD reads cleanly against the dark and leaves the lamp and ore glow to do the work. The cargo manifest floats bare over rock at the bottom right, and its icons and text lose contrast there.
Best screen: dark warm panel, bronze corner brackets, amber value hierarchy, glowing ore icons and a blurred world behind it. It fits the lamplit industrial tone.
Quiet and dignified, with a soft warm halo behind OUT, but it is plain text on black with no light or world imagery; it misses the core-floods-the-chamber feeling.

top_issues.issue: Title screen does not sell the descent
top_issues.why: The brief's title target is a dark shaft with a warm glow rising from far below and one small lit pod. Here the wordmark sits on an evenly lit mid-brown block wall, so there is no value gradient toward darkness and no light source underneath.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Darken the wall toward the top and edges and add a warm bloom rising from the bottom of the frame behind the wordmark, so the title is backlit by depth.

top_issues.issue: Title screen clutter under the CTA
top_issues.why: The bordered advance pill, the Steam link and the key legend compete with DESCEND and dilute the single-light, quiet mood.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Demote the advance line to plain dim text and lower the Steam link's contrast, keeping DESCEND as the only lit element.

top_issues.issue: Cargo manifest has no backing
top_issues.why: The cargo list sits directly on lit rock and glowing ore. Icon and text contrast varies with the terrain behind it, which hurts readability.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a faint dark vignette or gradient scrim behind the bottom-right HUD block, matching the shop panel's dark warm tone.

top_issues.issue: Fuel and hull bars are generic
top_issues.why: Flat web-style progress bars with tiny labels do not echo the bronze-bracket language of the shop panel, and the labels are hard to read.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Reuse the shop's bracket and frame motif on a slimmer panel, with slightly larger labels and a soft emissive edge on the fill.

top_issues.issue: Ending page has no light
top_issues.why: Light is the game's theme, yet the final page is text on near-black with only a faint halo.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Strengthen the warm glow into a slow-rising source behind the text, or add a faint core-light gradient from below, keeping the text quiet.

top_issues.issue: Glow halos are clipped to the tile square
top_issues.why: The brief wants emissives to bloom softly into the dark and light the stone around them. Hard square halos read as lit tiles, not light.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use a radial falloff that fades to zero before the tile edge, or let the bloom spill onto neighbouring rock faces.

top_issues.issue: Iron is nearly invisible at gameplay size
top_issues.why: Iron vs rock is a named pair. With no glow, it needs a value or colour step from the host rock, and in the dark it currently has none.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise the gunmetal-blue value and add a stronger, cooler specular rim or a few blue glints so it separates from the rock without glowing.

top_issues.issue: Nacre has the wrong silhouette
top_issues.why: The sheet calls for a scalloped, ribbed shell fan with pearly sheen. The spiky rosette collides with frostbloom, silver and diamond in the pale group.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Rebuild it as a flat, fan-shaped ribbed shell, keep the iridescent tint, and soften the glow toward a sheen.

top_issues.issue: The pale ores blur together at small size
top_issues.why: Silver, diamond, frostbloom and nacre all show as a white shape in a white-violet halo at ~50px.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give diamond an ice-blue tint or sparkle, remove silver's halo (metallic, no glow), and keep frostbloom's lavender distinct.

top_issues.issue: Gold reads as a yellow blob, not a split boulder
top_issues.why: The tell is rock with a golden wound; currently most of the mass is yellow.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make the outer mass dark rock, with gold showing in a crack or broken face that leaks the amber glow.
